cards.name: brush022
cards.summary: CorelDRAW Artistic Media Brush stroke (Objects category). Script render (the .cmx artwork mapped along an S-curve, not a shipped preview) shows about eight dark charcoal (RGB ~43,42,41) curved, pointed shards, each with open highlight cut-outs (the background shows through) like polished chrome, scattered as separate fragments along the path; glossy liquid-metal splash.
use_for: sci-fi, automotive or tech poster backgrounds
dynamic abstract trails behind a product
avoid: Clean line work or dividers: the fragments read as debris; use scroll15 or sensual14.
Thumbnail is a script approximation: multi-part brushes were combined into one curve with the first part's fill, so colours and tones in CorelDRAW may differ from what is shown.
Small sizes: the highlight cut-outs clog into black blobs.
cards.applies_to: open path or curve: the brush artwork is stretched along the path (draw with the Artistic Media tool or apply to a selected curve)
cards.how_to_apply: Artistic Media tool > Brush on the property bar > Category 'Objects' > Brush stroke 'brush022'; pick it before drawing, or select an existing curve and pick it to apply. Set thickness with the property bar's stroke width. Script: import the .cmx (C:\Program Files\Corel\CorelDRAW Graphics Suite\25\Draw\CustomMediaStrokes\Objects\brush022.cmx), size it, then Layer.CreateCurve(brush.Curve.CreateCurveMappedToStroke(path.Curve.SubPaths.Item(1), 1.0, False)); this maps the artwork as a plain curve with no live Artistic Media link (the route the thumbnail used).

verified.note: About seven or eight dark charcoal curved blade-like shards scattered along the S-curve, each with background-showing highlight cut-outs that read as chrome.

review.changes: summary: 'white highlight cut-outs' -> 'open highlight cut-outs (the background shows through)'
